answer.reason: The verses give only Enosh's birth, his fathering of Kenan, his age at death and his place in genealogies, which the summary already covers; the remark that men began to call on the LORD is a statement about men in his time, not a deed of his.
doubts: GEN 4:26 says 'then began men to call upon the name of the LORD', which is said of men generally and not clearly of Enosh himself, so it was not used.
